topic.title: AuditX DITA Information Architecture and Publishing Guide
topic.shortdesc: This document explains the DITA XML structure, single-sourcing strategy, audience profiling, and multi-channel publishing approach for AuditX documentation.

section.title: Overview: Single-Sourcing Strategy
section.p: AuditX documentation uses DITA (Darwin Information Typing Architecture) to implement true single-sourcing - one source, multiple outputs. This approach provides:

ul.li: Content Reusability: Topics are written once and reused across multiple guides
Audience Targeting: Metadata filters deliver content to appropriate user roles
Multi-Channel Support: Same source generates HTML, PDF, Help systems, and more
Consistency: Single source eliminates duplicate content and version control issues
Maintainability: Updates to one topic automatically propagate to all outputs

section.title: File Structure
section.p: AuditX DITA source files are organized as follows:

ul.li:
Concept Files (*.dita): Explain what something is
auditx-product-overview.dita - Product purpose and capabilities
auditx-workflows-overview.dita - Workflow types and selection guide

Task Files (*.dita): Explain how to do something
auditx-reset-password.dita - Password reset procedure
auditx-create-site.dita - Site creation steps
auditx-create-users.dita - User account creation
auditx-create-order-verification-workflow.dita - Workflow setup

Reference Files (*.dita): Contain structured factual information
auditx-user-roles.dita - Role definitions and permissions table
auditx-reports-reference.dita - Report fields and usage
auditx-glossary.dita - Term definitions
auditx-troubleshooting.dita - Solutions and support info

Map Files (*.ditamap): Assemble topics into deliverables
auditx-master.ditamap - All documentation in canonical order
auditx-admin-guide.ditamap - Administrator-focused content
auditx-supervisor-guide.ditamap - Supervisor/operations content
auditx-operator-guide.ditamap - Operator quick reference

section.title: Concept Topics
section.p: Purpose: Explain "what" and "why" - provide background, context, and understanding

ul.li: Product Overview (what is AuditX, key capabilities)
Workflows Overview (types of workflows, when to use each)

section.title: Task Topics
section.p: Purpose: Provide step-by-step instructions for accomplishing a goal

ul.li: Prereq - What must be done first
Steps - Numbered action steps with substeps
Result - What user should see/have after completing task

section.title: Reference Topics
section.p: Purpose: Provide lookup information, specifications, and detailed data

ul.li: Title - Noun phrase identifying information type
User Roles - Role definitions and permission matrix
Reports - Data field definitions and usage

section.title: Profiling Attributes
section.p: AuditX uses DITA profiling attributes to target content to specific audiences:

ul.li: <audience type="administrator"/> - System admins and IT staff

section.title: How Profiling Works
section.p: Audience metadata is placed in the <topicmeta> section of each topic reference in the map:
When publishing, the build process:

ol.li: Reads the audience attribute from the map
Includes/excludes the topic based on selected output audience

section.title: DITA Maps: Organizing for Multiple Deliverables
Master Map (auditx-master.ditamap)
section.p: Purpose: Single source of truth containing all AuditX documentation topics
Audience: Not used for direct publishing; serves as canonical reference
Content: All topics organized in logical order with all audience attributes
Use Case: Ensures completeness and consistency; used to generate multiple audience-specific maps

section.title: Administrator Guide (auditx-admin-guide.ditamap)
section.p: Purpose: Comprehensive guide for system administrators
Audience Filter: administrator, custom-user

ul.li: System Setup (site creation, user management, system configuration)

section.p: Excludes: Operator-only content, supervisor-only dashboards
Typical Output: PDF Administrator Manual, HTML Help Portal, Oxygen WebHelp

section.title: Supervisor Guide (auditx-supervisor-guide.ditamap)
section.p: Purpose: Reference for operations supervisors and managers
Audience Filter: supervisor
Excludes: Configuration tasks, admin functions, operator procedures
Typical Output: Quick Start PDF, Mobile-friendly HTML, Dashboard guide

section.title: Operator Guide (auditx-operator-guide.ditamap)
section.p: Purpose: Quick reference for packing floor operators
Audience Filter: operator
Excludes: All admin and configuration content
Typical Output: Laminated quick reference card, Mobile app, Touchscreen guide

section.title: Publishing Channels
section.p: The same DITA source content can be published to multiple output formats:

dd.p: Use Cases: Printing, offline reading, email distribution

ul.li: Administrator Manual (60+ pages, full index and TOC)
Supervisor Quick Start (10-15 pages, focused sections)
Operator Reference Card (2-4 pages, laminated format)

dd.p: Publishing Tool: Oxygen XML Editor, Apache FOP, or DITA OT
Use Cases: Web portal, help system, documentation site

ul.li: Integrated help system in Forge portal

dd.p: Publishing Tool: DITA Open Toolkit, Oxygen WebHelp
Use Cases: Mobile devices, tablets, responsive design
Publishing Tool: DITA OT with responsive plugin
Use Cases: In-application help, contextual assistance

section.title: Publishing Workflow
section.p: The typical DITA publishing workflow:

ol.li: Select Map: Choose audience-specific map (admin-guide, supervisor-guide, etc.)
Apply Filters: Specify audience profiling attributes to include/exclude
Choose Output Format: Select PDF, HTML, EPUB, or other format
Configure Output Settings: Set branding, colors, fonts, page layout
Generate: Run DITA processing to create deliverable
QA Review: Validate completeness and accuracy
Publish: Distribute to web, print, help system, or distribution channels

section.title: Publishing Command Examples
section.p: Using DITA Open Toolkit command line:
section.codeblock:
# Generate Administrator PDF dita -i auditx-admin-guide.ditamap -f pdf \ -Dargs.input.dir=/auditx-dita \ -Dargs.rellinks=none \ -o /output/auditx-admin-manual.pdf
# Generate Supervisor HTML dita -i auditx-supervisor-guide.ditamap -f html5 \ -Dargs.input.dir=/auditx-dita \ -o /output/supervisor-guide
# Generate Operator Quick Start (filtered) dita -i auditx-operator-guide.ditamap -f pdf \ -Dargs.filter=operator-filters.ditaval \ -o /output/operator-quick-ref.pdf

section.title: Example 1: Product Overview Reuse
section.p: The "Product Overview" concept appears in three different maps:

ul.li: Master Map: Canonical reference with all context
Admin Guide: Full version included in Part 1: Introduction
Supervisor Guide: Same topic included for supervisor understanding
Operator Guide: Same topic included for operator orientation

section.p: Benefit: When product capabilities change, update one topic and all guides automatically reflect the change.

section.title: Example 2: Workflow Overview Reuse
section.p: The "Workflows Overview" concept is included in multiple contexts:

ul.li: Admin Guide: Full version as Part 3: Configuring Workflows
Supervisor Guide: Included as read-only reference
Operator Guide: Simplified version for operator understanding

section.p: Benefit: Single topic maintains consistency across all guides while filtering may be used to show/hide implementation details.

section.title: Source Control Integration
section.p: DITA files should be maintained in a version control system (Git, Subversion, etc.):

ul.li: Track all changes to topics and maps
Maintain version history for audit purposes
Enable rollback to previous versions if needed

section.title: Update Process
section.p: When AuditX features change:

ol.li: Identify affected topics (e.g., workflow configuration topics)
Update source topics with new information
QA test all channels (PDF, HTML, Help system)

ul.li: Keep Topics Focused: Each topic should address one main topic/task
Use Consistent Structure: Follow DITA topic type patterns
Apply Metadata Correctly: Use profiling attributes to control visibility
Cross-Reference Carefully: Link related topics for navigation
Avoid Duplication: Reuse topics instead of copying content
Test Output: Verify all publishing channels generate correctly
Validate XML: Ensure DITA XML is well-formed and valid
Version Control: Commit changes regularly with meaningful messages
